clue.text: For nobs to get into public vehicle — a dreadful shock!

indicators.note: the nobs' letter is to go inside the vehicle's name, so this phrase signals a container

parts.note: a tram is a public vehicle running on rails
U is the label for upper-class usage, the speech of the nobs

explanation.surface: Posh passengers boarding a tram give everyone a terrible fright.
explanation.walkthrough: U as upper-class is a crossword convention from the U and non-U debate about British class speech; 'a' is a piece, not part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A trauma is a severe emotional blow, a deeply distressing experience.

clue.text: Go on bed inside which there's a rat!

indicators.note: in a down clue, on places the first piece above the second

parts.note: a turn is a go, as in a game

indicators.note: the a goes inside the bed word, a container

parts.note: a cot is a small bed

explanation.surface: Settling down in bed, someone discovers a rodent in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inside which' puts A in COT to make COAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A rat is a traitor or defector, one who changes sides.

clue.text: On wing over the sea, like Icarus as wax melted?

indicators.note: in a down clue, over places the first piece above the second

parts.note: alar means relating to wings
the Med is the Mediterranean Sea

explanation.surface: Flying over the Mediterranean, Icarus panicked as his wings came apart.
explanation.walkthrough: Icarus flew too near the sun on wings of feathers and wax; the wax melted and he fell into the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Alarmed means frightened, as Icarus would be when his wings began to fail.

clue.text: Frantic salesperson with valuable material —- coral

parts.note: mad means frantic
a rep is a sales representative
ore is the rock mined for valuable metal

explanation.surface: A frenzied seller has precious coral to offer.
explanation.definitionFit: Madrepore is a reef-building stony coral.

clue.text: Remove concrete? No

definitions.meaning: to take away or extract something, as a verb
the opposite of concrete is theoretical, not physical

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests digging out concrete; one sense is the verb meaning extract, the other the adjective that is the opposite of concrete.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to extract; as an adjective it means theoretical, the antonym of concrete.

clue.text: Sentence starts or ends here? It's immaterial

definitions.meaning: a written sentence ends at a full point and the next starts right next to it
something irrelevant to the matter at hand

explanation.walkthrough: The first reading takes the phrase literally: beside the full stop that marks a sentence's end.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means irrelevant; literally it places a sentence's edge next to its full stop.

clue.text: One goes underground to counter uprising

indicators.note: in a down clue, an uprising means the word is read from the bottom up

parts.note: to rebut is to counter an argument

explanation.surface: A secret agent goes underground to fight a rebellion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uprising' turns REBUT upward.
explanation.definitionFit: A tuber, such as a potato, is a swollen stem growing underground.

clue.text: Man with hesitation when meeting students? He was one himself

parts.note: Al is a man's name
um is a hesitant sound
NUS is the National Union of Students, the British student body

explanation.surface: A man hesitates on meeting students, having once been a student too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He was one himself' refers back to students, the definition borrowing the clue's own word.
explanation.definitionFit: An alumnus is a former student of a school or university.

clue.text: Beast not allowing son to mess about

indicators.note: the beast word refuses entry to the son letter, removing it

parts.note: a stinker is a nasty person, a beast

explanation.surface: A brute won't let a boy play around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not allowing' removes S from STINKER.
explanation.definitionFit: To tinker is to fiddle or mess about with something.

clue.text: It's converted for traipses indeed!

indicators.note: the letters are converted into a new order, an anagram signal

explanation.surface: A street has been changed to suit people who trudge on foot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'converted' rearranges TRAIPSES and INDEED; the whole clue describes a road given over to walkers.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedestrianised street is converted for walkers only, closed to traffic.

clue.text: Look over gear and tackle again

parts.note: to read something is to look over it
dress is clothing, gear

explanation.surface: Someone inspects their kit before having another go at a job.
explanation.definitionFit: To readdress a problem is to deal with it once more, tackling it a second time.

clue.text: Collapse when following black bear

indicators.note: the collapse word comes after the black letter, so this phrase orders the charade

parts.note: B is the standard abbreviation for black, as on pencils
ruin as a noun means collapse or downfall

explanation.surface: A black bear falls down.
explanation.definitionFit: Bruin is a traditional nickname for a bear, from the bear in the Reynard fables.

clue.text: Presenter of match broadcast

indicators.note: something broadcast is heard, so the word is taken by how it is said

parts.note: to compare is to match one thing against another

explanation.surface: The host of a televised football game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' fits the surface's TV match but signals that the word is heard rather than read.
explanation.definitionFit: A compere is the host who introduces acts on a show, a presenter.

clue.text: Disorder and risk reduced when Queen is involved

indicators.note: the Queen's letters are wrapped up inside the shortened word, signalling a container
the risk word is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: danger means risk
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: Chaos ensues, with less danger once the monarch takes part.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'Disorder and risk' as a pair, but 'Disorder' alone is the definition and 'and' a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To derange is to throw into disorder, to disturb the arrangement of something.

clue.text: Typist in a workshop losing stones

indicators.note: the workshop word drops letters, so losing signals a deletion

parts.note: a studio is an artist's workshop
st is the abbreviation for stone, the British weight, used for the plural too

explanation.surface: A secretary working in a studio has shed some weight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing' takes ST from STUDIO, leaving UDIO. A stone is a British unit of body weight, 14 pounds.
explanation.definitionFit: An audio typist transcribes recordings, so the word stands for that kind of typist.

clue.text: Put various items out for bird

indicators.note: the letters are put into various arrangements, an anagram signal

explanation.surface: Leave assorted things outside for the birds to find.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put various' rearranges ITEMS and OUT.
explanation.definitionFit: A titmouse is a small songbird, the tit.

clue.text: Like illicit relationship — away from the main dish!

definitions.meaning: describes a secret affair carried on besides a marriage
served separately as an accompaniment, as a side dish is

explanation.walkthrough: One sense is an affair conducted secretly; the other is food served as a side order.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means secretly, of an affair, and as a separate accompaniment, of food.

clue.text: Most puritanical maidens being hugged by cleric

indicators.note: the maidens are held inside the cleric word, a container

parts.note: a priest is a cleric
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over, so two are MM

explanation.surface: Young women embraced by a clergyman, the strictest possible.
explanation.walkthrough: A maiden in cricket is an over with no runs scored.
explanation.definitionFit: Primmest is the superlative of prim, most strait-laced and proper.

clue.text: Cat past 51 — is it making use of its ninth?

definitions.text: is it making use of its ninth?

indicators.note: the cat word comes after the number, so past orders the charade

parts.note: LI is 51 in Roman numerals
a feline is a cat

explanation.surface: An elderly cat may be down to the last of its nine lives.
explanation.walkthrough: Cats are said to have nine lives; one on its ninth is clinging to its last chance.
explanation.definitionFit: A lifeline is a last means of rescue, as the final of a cat's nine lives would be.

clue.text: Dictator — present identification and you'll find me at home!

parts.note: spoken by someone at home: I am in

explanation.surface: A tyrant demands papers and says he'll be at home.
explanation.walkthrough: IDI AMIN was the military dictator of Uganda in the 1970s.
explanation.definitionFit: Idi Amin was Uganda's brutal military dictator from 1971 to 1979.

clue.text: One may have the minutes to send back

indicators.note: the send word is read backwards

parts.note: to remit is to send money or papers

explanation.surface: A committee secretary must return the meeting's minutes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns REMIT around. The minutes are those counted, not a meeting's record.
explanation.definitionFit: A timer holds and counts down minutes, as a kitchen timer does.

clue.text: This person -—- possibly chief con-tributer to global warming

parts.note: the speaker, me
a thane was a clan chief in Scotland, one example of a chief

explanation.surface: I am perhaps the main cause of climate change.
explanation.walkthrough: A THANE was a Scottish lord or clan chief, as Macbeth was.
explanation.definitionFit: Methane is a potent greenhouse gas contributing to global warming.

clue.text: Stop talking in prison?

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is both a command to be silent and a description of being locked up.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a curt order to be quiet, and also means confined or locked away.

clue.text: Bit of metal stuck in a lock?

definitions.text: Bit of metal stuck in a lock?

parts.words: Bit of metal stuck in a lock?
parts.note: suggests a burglar's pick jammed in a door lock, but the lock is a lock of hair held by a bent wire

explanation.walkthrough: The lock is hair, not a door's mechanism.
explanation.definitionFit: A U-shaped wire pin pushed into the hair holds a lock of it in place.

clue.text: Fly perhaps landing on egg sauce

indicators.note: in a down clue, landing on puts the first piece above the second

parts.note: a fly is an example of a pest
O looks like an egg

explanation.surface: A fly settles on an egg dish's sauce.
explanation.definitionFit: Pesto is an Italian sauce of basil, pine nuts and cheese.

clue.text: Fold when the first bit of impetus disappears

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the impetus word is affected
that opening letter is removed, signalling a deletion

parts.note: momentum means impetus, driving force

explanation.surface: A business folds when it loses its initial drive.
explanation.definitionFit: The omentum is a fold of the peritoneum in the abdomen, an anatomical fold.

clue.text: Books from the paper one found to be old

indicators.note: the one letter is found to be replaced by the old letter, a substitution

parts.note: The Times is the newspaper, this puzzle's own
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Volumes from the newspaper, one of which turns out to be ancient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found to be' swaps I for O in TIMES.
explanation.definitionFit: Tomes are books, especially large heavy volumes.

clue.text: Nicest day out for a business group

indicators.note: the letters are put out of order, an anagram signal

explanation.surface: The best day away for a company outing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges NICEST and DAY.
explanation.definitionFit: A syndicate is an association of businesses formed for a joint venture.

clue.text: Find fault with badly dressed pudding

parts.note: to pan is to criticise harshly
dowdy means shabbily or unfashionably dressed

explanation.surface: Criticise a dessert that has been poorly presented.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' looks like an anagram signal but 'badly dressed' is one piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A pandowdy is an American baked apple pudding with a crust.

clue.text: Fellow pushed back after monarch's return?

definitions.text: Fellow pushed back after monarch's return?

indicators.note: the fellow word is placed behind the other piece, ordering the charade
the monarch's letters are turned around

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the monarch
gent is short for gentleman, a fellow

explanation.surface: A man is sidelined once the king or queen comes home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' turns ER into RE. The whole clue also describes a stand-in ruler whose power ends when the monarch returns.
explanation.definitionFit: A regent rules in a monarch's absence and steps aside on the monarch's return.
